rules.title: Dwelling house (standard lot): maximum building height 9.5 m and 2 storeys
rules.instrument: Brisbane City Plan 2014 (v37.00/2026)

source_detail.quote: AO2 Development in the Low density residential zone, Character residential zone, ... results in a maximum building height of 9.5m and: - 2 storeys; or - 1 storey if ...
source_detail.text:
AO2
Development in the Low density residential zone, Character residential zone, 2 storey mix zone precinct of the Low–medium density residential zone, Rural residential zone, Environmental management zone, Rural zone or Emerging community zone results in a maximum building height of 9.5m and:
- 2 storeys; or
- 1 storey if the development also includes a space that is situated between one floor level and the floor level next above, or if there is no floor above, the ceiling or roof above that contains only a bathroom, shower room, laundry, water closet, or other sanitary compartment.
Editor's note—This acceptable outcome is only for the maximum building height. Side boundary setbacks are provided in accordance with the Queensland Development Code; which vary according to the height of the building.
Editor's note—For the purposes of determining compliance with AO2 reference is to be made to section 1.7.7.

rules.interpretation_notes: Table 1.6.1 item 6: a s32(b) quantifiable standard for QDC MP1.1/1.2 performance criteria 4 (height) — replaces QDC A4 (8.5 m) for building assessment. Applies to domestic outbuildings only through the dwelling house definition; Brisbane has no separate outbuilding height cap here, so the QHC/QDC 4.5 m Class 10a limit is not applicable while MP 1.2 applies (MP 1.2 has none).

rules.instrument: Brisbane City Plan 2014 (v37.00/2026)

source_detail.quote: Development for a building which is not on a rear lot is set back from any road alignment, excluding eaves, awnings, stairs and garage, within 20% of the average front setback of the nearest residential buildings constructed in 1946 or earlier fronting the same street.
source_detail.text:
If in the Low-medium density residential zone or the Character residential zone, where for a dwelling house, dual occupancy, multiple dwelling, retirement facility, rooming accommodation, or short-term accommodation, where not in the Local character significance sub-category |
AO1.2
Development for a building which is not on a rear lot is set back from any road alignment, excluding eaves, awnings, stairs and garage, within 20% of the average front setback of the nearest residential buildings constructed in 1946 or earlier fronting the same street.
Note—Additional buildings by way of infill development may be set further back on this site, subject to meeting other code requirements. Where the site contains a building constructed in 1946 or earlier, it should be retained at the front of the site and any new infill placed behind/beside. Sliding a building constructed in 1946 or earlier back with infill at the front of the site is not consistent with desired traditional setting outcomes.

rules.interpretation_notes: 'Within 20%' is a band: setback must be between 0.8x and 1.2x the average. The minimum (0.8x) is encoded; the 1.2x maximum is noted for the geometry layer. Automatable once pre1946_neighbour_avg_front_setback_m is supplied (a site/aerial-photo determination of the nearest pre-1946 houses' setbacks -- never auto-derivable, see research 2026-11-05: no text schedule, no per-building GIS layer, no building-age dataset exists for Brisbane); otherwise still manual review.

rules.title: Class 10a wall within 900 mm of a boundary (not a road) or 1.8 m of another building must be fire-separated construction
rules.instrument: National Construction Code (NCC 2022, adopted Housing Provisions (Volume Two equivalent))

source_detail.quote: The Class 1 building must be protected ... where a Class 10a building is between or adjacent to it and a boundary (other than a boundary adjoining a road alignment or open space) -- protection options include: the Class 10a building is not less than 900 mm from the allotment boundary (setback); or, where the Class 10a wall is less than 900 mm from the boundary, that wall complies with 9.2.3.
source_detail.text: 9.2.4(1)(a) The Class 1 building must be protected under 9.2.5 where a Class 10a building is between or adjacent to it and a boundary (other than a boundary adjoining a road alignment or open space). 9.2.5 protection options include: the Class 10a building is not less than 900 mm from the allotment boundary (setback); or, where the Class 10a wall is less than 900 mm from the boundary, that wall complies with 9.2.3.

source_detail.quote: The Class 1 building must be protected ... where the Class 10a building is between or adjacent to it and another building on the same allotment -- protection options include: the Class 10a building is not less than 1.8 m from the other building (separation); or, where the Class 10a wall is less than 1.8 m from the other building, that wall complies with 9.2.3.
source_detail.text: 9.2.4(1)(b) The Class 1 building must be protected under 9.2.6 where the Class 10a building is between or adjacent to it and another building on the same allotment. 9.2.6 protection options include: the Class 10a building is not less than 1.8 m from the other building (separation); or, where the Class 10a wall is less than 1.8 m from the other building, that wall complies with 9.2.3.

rules.interpretation_notes: Deliberately NOT a siting/setback rule -- it is a construction standard that applies whatever the final built distance turns out to be under the siting rules elsewhere in this report, including where a council/QDC/QHC relaxation already permits 0 m (built-to-boundary). It only bites once the structure is actually sited within 900 mm of a side/rear boundary (never a road boundary) or within 1.8 m of another building on the same allotment (e.g. the house) -- confirm the proposed wall's actual distance and, if within those thresholds, its construction against 9.2.3 (or use the 9.2.8 open-carport exemption). Always surfaced for a Class 10a structure since the tool does not know the final as-sited distance in advance; always MANUAL_REVIEW for the same reason. Does not apply to Class 10b (pools) -- pool fencing is covered separately (QDC MP 3.4, rule family MP34.*).

rules.title: Swimming pool side and rear boundary clearance (from water's edge)
rules.instrument: QDC MP 1.2 - Design and siting standard for single detached housing - on lots 450m2 and over (Publication date 11 March 2010)

source_detail.text: (a) The side and rear boundary clearance for a part of the building or structure is – (i) where the height of that part is 4.5m or less - 1.5m; and (ii) where the height of that part is greater than 4.5m but not more than 7.5m - 2m; and (iii) where the height is greater that 7.5m - 2m plus 0.5m for every 3m or part exceeding 7.5m.

rules.interpretation_notes: A2(a) applies to 'a part of the building or structure'; a pool is a structure and the side and rear boundary clearance for a pool is measured from the water's edge. Height of the pool part taken as coping height above natural ground. Full 3-tier A2(a) formula applied by height (<=4.5m / <=7.5m / taller), matching A2a.SIDE_REAR_CLEARANCE - the previous version only encoded the first tier and returned null (manual review) above 4.5 m, which was an incomplete encoding, not a real legal distinction (the quoted clause is the same one applied to any part of any structure).

rules.title: Regulated pool must have a continuous barrier restricting young children's access
rules.instrument: QDC MP 3.4 - Swimming pool barriers (Publication date 18 July 2012)

source_detail.text: Swimming pools must have a barrier which: (a) is continuous for the full extent of the hazard; and (b) is of a strength and rigidity to withstand the foreseeable impact of people; and (c) restricts the access of young children to the pool and the immediate pool surrounds, including access from class 1, 2 or 3 buildings or class 4 parts of buildings located within or outside the pool area; and (d) has any gates fitted with latching devices not readily operated by young children, and constructed to automatically close and latch; and (e) except for indoor swimming pools, does not incorporate any doors providing access to or from a building.

rules.interpretation_notes: Continuity from plan geometry can be screened (closed ring around pool area) but final compliance needs a pool safety certificate (Building Act s234).

source_detail.quote: AO2 Development in the Low density residential zone, Character residential zone, ... results in a maximum building height of 9.5m and: - 2 storeys; or - 1 storey if ...
source_detail.text:
AO2
Development in the Low density residential zone, Character residential zone, 2 storey mix zone precinct of the Low–medium density residential zone, Rural residential zone, Environmental management zone, Rural zone or Emerging community zone results in a maximum building height of 9.5m and:
- 2 storeys; or
- 1 storey if the development also includes a space that is situated between one floor level and the floor level next above, or if there is no floor above, the ceiling or roof above that contains only a bathroom, shower room, laundry, water closet, or other sanitary compartment.

source_detail.text: 9.2.4(1)(a) The Class 1 building must be protected under 9.2.5 where a Class 10a building is between or adjacent to it and a boundary (other than a boundary adjoining a road alignment or open space). 9.2.5 protection options include: the Class 10a building is not less than 900 mm from the allotment boundary (setback); or, where the Class 10a wall is less than 900 mm from the boundary, that wall complies with 9.2.3.

source_detail.quote: The Class 1 building must be protected ... where the Class 10a building is between or adjacent to it and another building on the same allotment -- protection options include: the Class 10a building is not less than 1.8 m from the other building (separation); or, where the Class 10a wall is less than 1.8 m from the other building, that wall complies with 9.2.3.
source_detail.text: 9.2.4(1)(b) The Class 1 building must be protected under 9.2.6 where the Class 10a building is between or adjacent to it and another building on the same allotment. 9.2.6 protection options include: the Class 10a building is not less than 1.8 m from the other building (separation); or, where the Class 10a wall is less than 1.8 m from the other building, that wall complies with 9.2.3.

rules.interpretation_notes: Deliberately NOT a siting/setback rule -- it is a construction standard that applies whatever the final built distance turns out to be under the siting rules elsewhere in this report, including where a council/QDC/QHC relaxation already permits 0 m (built-to-boundary). It only bites once the structure is actually sited within 900 mm of a side/rear boundary (never a road boundary) or within 1.8 m of another building on the same allotment (e.g. the house) -- confirm the proposed wall's actual distance and, if within those thresholds, its construction against 9.2.3 (or use the 9.2.8 open-carport exemption). Always surfaced for a Class 10a structure since the tool does not know the final as-sited distance in advance; always MANUAL_REVIEW for the same reason. Always surfaced for a Class 10a structure since the tool does not know the final as-sited distance in advance; always MANUAL_REVIEW for the same reason. rules.title: Class 10a wall within 900 mm of a boundary (not a road) or 1.8 m of another building must be fire-separated construction
rules.instrument: National Construction Code (NCC 2022, adopted Housing Provisions (Volume Two equivalent))

source_detail.quote: The Class 1 building must be protected ... where a Class 10a building is between or adjacent to it and a boundary (other than a boundary adjoining a road alignment or open space) -- protection options include: the Class 10a building is not less than 900 mm from the allotment boundary (setback); or, where the Class 10a wall is less than 900 mm from the boundary, that wall complies with 9.2.3.
source_detail.text: 9.2.4(1)(a) The Class 1 building must be protected under 9.2.5 where a Class 10a building is between or adjacent to it and a boundary (other than a boundary adjoining a road alignment or open space). 9.2.5 protection options include: the Class 10a building is not less than 900 mm from the allotment boundary (setback); or, where the Class 10a wall is less than 900 mm from the boundary, that wall complies with 9.2.3.

source_detail.quote: The Class 1 building must be protected ... where the Class 10a building is between or adjacent to it and another building on the same allotment -- protection options include: the Class 10a building is not less than 1.8 m from the other building (separation); or, where the Class 10a wall is less than 1.8 m from the other building, that wall complies with 9.2.3.
source_detail.text: 9.2.4(1)(b) The Class 1 building must be protected under 9.2.6 where the Class 10a building is between or adjacent to it and another building on the same allotment. 9.2.6 protection options include: the Class 10a building is not less than 1.8 m from the other building (separation); or, where the Class 10a wall is less than 1.8 m from the other building, that wall complies with 9.2.3.

rules.interpretation_notes: Deliberately NOT a siting/setback rule -- it is a construction standard that applies whatever the final built distance turns out to be under the siting rules elsewhere in this report, including where a council/QDC/QHC relaxation already permits 0 m (built-to-boundary). It only bites once the structure is actually sited within 900 mm of a side/rear boundary (never a road boundary) or within 1.8 m of another building on the same allotment (e.g. the house) -- confirm the proposed wall's actual distance and, if within those thresholds, its construction against 9.2.3 (or use the 9.2.8 open-carport exemption). Always surfaced for a Class 10a structure since the tool does not know the final as-sited distance in advance; always MANUAL_REVIEW for the same reason. Does not apply to Class 10b (pools) -- pool fencing is covered separately (QDC MP 3.4, rule family MP34.*).

rules.instrument: National Construction Code (NCC 2022, adopted Housing Provisions (Volume Two equivalent))

source_detail.quote: The Class 1 building must be protected ... where a Class 10a building is between or adjacent to it and a boundary (other than a boundary adjoining a road alignment or open space) -- protection options include: the Class 10a building is not less than 900 mm from the allotment boundary (setback); or, where the Class 10a wall is less than 900 mm from the boundary, that wall complies with 9.2.3.
source_detail.text: 9.2.4(1)(a) The Class 1 building must be protected under 9.2.5 where a Class 10a building is between or adjacent to it and a boundary (other than a boundary adjoining a road alignment or open space). 9.2.5 protection options include: the Class 10a building is not less than 900 mm from the allotment boundary (setback); or, where the Class 10a wall is less than 900 mm from the boundary, that wall complies with 9.2.3.

source_detail.quote: The Class 1 building must be protected ... where the Class 10a building is between or adjacent to it and another building on the same allotment -- protection options include: the Class 10a building is not less than 1.8 m from the other building (separation); or, where the Class 10a wall is less than 1.8 m from the other building, that wall complies with 9.2.3.
source_detail.text: 9.2.4(1)(b) The Class 1 building must be protected under 9.2.6 where the Class 10a building is between or adjacent to it and another building on the same allotment. 9.2.6 protection options include: the Class 10a building is not less than 1.8 m from the other building (separation); or, where the Class 10a wall is less than 1.8 m from the other building, that wall complies with 9.2.3.

rules.interpretation_notes: Deliberately NOT a siting/setback rule -- it is a construction standard that applies whatever the final built distance turns out to be under the siting rules elsewhere in this report, including where a council/QDC/QHC relaxation already permits 0 m (built-to-boundary). It only bites once the structure is actually sited within 900 mm of a side/rear boundary (never a road boundary) or within 1.8 m of another building on the same allotment (e.g. the house) -- confirm the proposed wall's actual distance and, if within those thresholds, its construction against 9.2.3 (or use the 9.2.8 open-carport exemption). Always surfaced for a Class 10a structure since the tool does not know the final as-sited distance in advance; always MANUAL_REVIEW for the same reason. Does not apply to Class 10b (pools) -- pool fencing is covered separately (QDC MP 3.4, rule family MP34.*).

Compare against this structure's own floor area (plan_area_m2 in the engine), not a running total of existing + new outbuildings.

rules.title: Class 10a wall within 900 mm of a boundary (not a road) or 1.8 m of another building must be fire-separated construction
rules.instrument: National Construction Code (NCC 2022, adopted Housing Provisions (Volume Two equivalent))

source_detail.quote: The Class 1 building must be protected ... where a Class 10a building is between or adjacent to it and a boundary (other than a boundary adjoining a road alignment or open space) -- protection options include: the Class 10a building is not less than 900 mm from the allotment boundary (setback); or, where the Class 10a wall is less than 900 mm from the boundary, that wall complies with 9.2.3.
source_detail.text: 9.2.4(1)(a) The Class 1 building must be protected under 9.2.5 where a Class 10a building is between or adjacent to it and a boundary (other than a boundary adjoining a road alignment or open space). 9.2.5 protection options include: the Class 10a building is not less than 900 mm from the allotment boundary (setback); or, where the Class 10a wall is less than 900 mm from the boundary, that wall complies with 9.2.3.

source_detail.quote: The Class 1 building must be protected ... where the Class 10a building is between or adjacent to it and another building on the same allotment -- protection options include: the Class 10a building is not less than 1.8 m from the other building (separation); or, where the Class 10a wall is less than 1.8 m from the other building, that wall complies with 9.2.3.
source_detail.text: 9.2.4(1)(b) The Class 1 building must be protected under 9.2.6 where the Class 10a building is between or adjacent to it and another building on the same allotment. 9.2.6 protection options include: the Class 10a building is not less than 1.8 m from the other building (separation); or, where the Class 10a wall is less than 1.8 m from the other building, that wall complies with 9.2.3.

rules.interpretation_notes: Deliberately NOT a siting/setback rule -- it is a construction standard that applies whatever the final built distance turns out to be under the siting rules elsewhere in this report, including where a council/QDC/QHC relaxation already permits 0 m (built-to-boundary). It only bites once the structure is actually sited within 900 mm of a side/rear boundary (never a road boundary) or within 1.8 m of another building on the same allotment (e.g. the house) -- confirm the proposed wall's actual distance and, if within those thresholds, its construction against 9.2.3 (or use the 9.2.8 open-carport exemption). Always surfaced for a Class 10a structure since the tool does not know the final as-sited distance in advance; always MANUAL_REVIEW for the same reason. Does not apply to Class 10b (pools) -- pool fencing is covered separately (QDC MP 3.4, rule family MP34.*).

rules.title: Class 10a wall within 900 mm of a boundary (not a road) or 1.8 m of another building must be fire-separated construction
rules.instrument: National Construction Code (NCC 2022, adopted Housing Provisions (Volume Two equivalent))

source_detail.quote: The Class 1 building must be protected ... where a Class 10a building is between or adjacent to it and a boundary (other than a boundary adjoining a road alignment or open space) -- protection options include: the Class 10a building is not less than 900 mm from the allotment boundary (setback); or, where the Class 10a wall is less than 900 mm from the boundary, that wall complies with 9.2.3.
source_detail.text: 9.2.4(1)(a) The Class 1 building must be protected under 9.2.5 where a Class 10a building is between or adjacent to it and a boundary (other than a boundary adjoining a road alignment or open space). 9.2.5 protection options include: the Class 10a building is not less than 900 mm from the allotment boundary (setback); or, where the Class 10a wall is less than 900 mm from the boundary, that wall complies with 9.2.3.

source_detail.quote: The Class 1 building must be protected ... where the Class 10a building is between or adjacent to it and another building on the same allotment -- protection options include: the Class 10a building is not less than 1.8 m from the other building (separation); or, where the Class 10a wall is less than 1.8 m from the other building, that wall complies with 9.2.3.
source_detail.text: 9.2.4(1)(b) The Class 1 building must be protected under 9.2.6 where the Class 10a building is between or adjacent to it and another building on the same allotment. 9.2.6 protection options include: the Class 10a building is not less than 1.8 m from the other building (separation); or, where the Class 10a wall is less than 1.8 m from the other building, that wall complies with 9.2.3.

rules.interpretation_notes: Deliberately NOT a siting/setback rule -- it is a construction standard that applies whatever the final built distance turns out to be under the siting rules elsewhere in this report, including where a council/QDC/QHC relaxation already permits 0 m (built-to-boundary). It only bites once the structure is actually sited within 900 mm of a side/rear boundary (never a road boundary) or within 1.8 m of another building on the same allotment (e.g. the house) -- confirm the proposed wall's actual distance and, if within those thresholds, its construction against 9.2.3 (or use the 9.2.8 open-carport exemption). Always surfaced for a Class 10a structure since the tool does not know the final as-sited distance in advance; always MANUAL_REVIEW for the same reason. Does not apply to Class 10b (pools) -- pool fencing is covered separately (QDC MP 3.4, rule family MP34.*).
